Think Your Conscious Brain Directs Your Actions? Think Again

I actually brought up this particular paper about a month ago, but it's worth revisiting again, especially when there's new information from Singularity Hub. It's very revolutionary in terms of AI, but I think it also is largely correct -- and right here in SFSU. It's the study of consciousness, of what makes up specifically human, but it basically says that it's very similar to every other animal -- much more than is generally believed...

I'm failing to see what the evidence is here for the "Passive Frame Theory". Isn't it just an assumption that all we can know about consciousness is through behavior? This guy is simply ignoring intentions, motivations and emotions all together. I bet he's a blast at parties.

This takes into account intentions, motivations, and emotions; they are all unconscious. I don't necessarily think this theory must be 100% correct, but it is interesting. It's not like we have a remotely good handle on consciousness anyways.

This makes a lot of sense if you think of consciousness as a condition monitoring system rather than as control logic. Your subconscious brain does all of your decision making, information processing and so on. Your conscious self sits back and watches the outcome, analysing what you did right or wrong and how to change your approach next time.

1) What were my expectations going into the arc?

I already knew what was coming. I read spoilers. I live spoilers. I love spoilers. I will read the entire wiki for a show before I touch the first episode. I enjoy more how the story and twists are presented. Knowing what the story and twists are is generally how I determine if a show is worth my time. But yes, I would dare say that the this arc "exceeded expectations."

2) What did I think of the class rep's transformation near the end?

First off, kudos to a show for having an actual, viable psychopath. This isn't your standard yandere, and this isn't your standard tsundere. Psychopaths play a part in order to appear "normal", but underneath that veneer is something a bit more sinister.

Secondly, this arc is an important PSA on the importance of effective communication. A lot of the conflicts are essentially a break down in communication and one side jumping towards an extreme conclusion. In pretty much all cases, it was Ayatsuji who was behind the major misunderstandings which in turn led to a major malfunction.

I'd say this is probably my second favorite arc of them all, simply due it being relatively unexplored waters in the field of anime romance. You have shows that attempt some of these elements, but none that do it quite as well.

The return of Azusa's i Love for the closing session of episode 24 was, in a word, masterfully done. Amagami SS is a show where it's kinda easy to lose your place, given how many arcs you burn through - one might even consider Amagami SS to be six shows in one, and in a way it is.
